info.title: eBPFsentinel Agent API
info.description:
REST API for the eBPFsentinel network security agent.

Provides endpoints for managing firewall rules, IPS/IDS policies, rate limiting, L7 filtering, threat intelligence, alerts, and audit logs.

Most endpoints require authentication via JWT Bearer token or API key.

get.description:
Server-side filtering happens on every alert before it is forwarded.
Reconnects can pass `Last-Event-ID` to backfill missed alerts from
the in-memory replay buffer (≤ 5 000 events). Lagged subscribers
silently skip the gap; clients should refetch via
`GET /api/v1/alerts` to backfill in that case.

`GET /api/v1/conntrack/events` - Server-Sent Events stream of
conntrack lifecycle events (new / update / destroy).
get.description:
The poller diffs conntrack snapshots every 2 s and
pushes changes into a broadcast channel. Each SSE client receives
a copy. Lagged clients silently skip missed events.

200.description: SSE stream of `event: new`, `event: update` and `event: destroy` frames. Each frame's `data` is one JSON object carrying `event_type` and the `connection` it happened to; `:keepalive` is sent every 15 s.

post.summary: `POST /api/v1/trace` - what the loaded programs decide for one packet.
post.description:
A packet is crafted from the five-tuple and run through the programs in
the order the hooks run them, with no interface and no traffic. Every
program reads its maps and skips its writes, so a trace changes no state.
A verdict that depends on state the crafted packet does not carry, an
established connection or a rate already spent, is reported as such.

200.description: Each stage the packet crossed and where it stopped

400.description: The request does not describe one packet, or the workload has no address

503.description: The kernel refused to run the programs

AgentIdentityResponse.description:
Operator-managed metadata advertised to the dashboard, plus the
minimum identity fields needed to identify the agent uniquely.

Read-only view of the agent's `management` config block; both fields
are hot-reloadable via the existing config reload mechanism.

hostname.description: `gethostname()` at startup; surfaces the host running the agent.

operator_endpoint.description:
Optional URL the operator exposes (typically a Kubernetes-native
UI). The dashboard deep-links to this URL from the
"operator-managed" badge.

operator_managed.description:
`true` when the agent's configuration is owned by the Kubernetes
operator (CRD-driven). The dashboard locks its config-edit UI on
agents reporting `true` to prevent two-way drift.

version.description: Build version of the running agent (`CARGO_PKG_VERSION`).

config.description: Which document is running and what changed the policy since.

container_coverage.description: What the agent sees of the containers on this node.

status.description:
Coarse lifecycle state: `running` once eBPF programs are attached,
`degraded` while operating without them (userspace-only fallback).

AlertNoteResponse.description: One note on an alert as the API writes it.

author.description: Who the caller said wrote it.

via.description: The identity the agent authenticated the write under.

oneOf.description: Container identity resolved from the event's `cgroup_id` (if any).

data_type.description: DLP: data category (pci, pii, credentials, custom).

executable_dev.description: DLP: device number of that binary, present with `executable_path`.

executable_inode.description:
DLP: inode of that binary, present with `executable_path`. The pair
identifies the file even where the path was reused.

executable_path.description:
DLP: the binary the writing process was running, read from
`/proc/<pid>/exe` at alert time. Absent when the process was already
gone, which is the honest answer rather than a guessed name.

executable_source.description: DLP: how the executable was obtained - `process_at_alert_time`.

flow_source.description:
DLP: how the five-tuple was obtained - `kernel_socket` when the probe
read it off the socket, `task_socket_correlation` when it came from
the same task's last socket. Absent means the addresses and ports are
zero because nothing was resolved, not because the peer is 0.0.0.0.

mitigation_status.description:
What was done about the source: a `DDoS` mitigation state, or the
outcome of blocking the source of an application attack.

notes.description: What people wrote on it, oldest first.

src_addr.description:
Source address as four big-endian u32 words.
IPv4: `[v4, 0, 0, 0]`. IPv6: full 128-bit address.

status.description: Where the alert stands in the queue; `open` until somebody moves it.

triage_updated_ns.description: When the triage last changed (nanoseconds since epoch).

oneOf.description:
The process behind the flow, where the node could name one. Absent
for a flow it only forwarded, for a socket opened before the hooks
attached, and on a host whose kernel refused them.

AttachBlockEntry.description: One attach the kernel refused, and what is standing in the way.

nested_xdp.description:
True when the interface already carries somebody else's XDP program,
the nested-XDP case that Docker and Kubernetes produce.

reason.description:
Operator-readable sentence: what the kernel said, translated against
what is actually on the interface right now.

AttributionReport.description: What became of the cgroup socket hooks on this host.

attached.description:
True only when every hook attached. A partial set is reported as not
attached, because half the hooks make an absent workload mean two
different things with nothing on the wire to tell them apart.

brokered.description: Whether the warden created the links, which is the rootless posture.

cgroup.description: The cgroup the hooks were attached to, or asked for.

hooks.description: The hooks that attached, named as the kernel programs are.

reason.description: Why nothing is attached, in the words the attach failed with.

src_addr.description:
Source address as four big-endian u32 words.
IPv4: `[v4, 0, 0, 0]`. IPv6: full 128-bit address.

BpfLsmReport.description: Whether the BPF LSM runs on this host, and what would make it run.

active.description: `bpf` is among the active security modules.

built.description:
Whether the kernel was built with the BPF LSM, read from its BTF.
Absent when the BTF could not be read, which proves nothing either way.

modules.description:
The active security modules in the order the kernel runs them, empty
when the list could not be read.

reason.description: Why an LSM program cannot attach here, in one sentence.

remedy.description: What would make it attach, in one sentence.

BulkTriageRequest.description: `POST /api/v1/alerts/triage` body: one change applied to many alerts.

missing.description: Alerts the store no longer holds.

updated.description: Alerts the change was applied to.

CapabilityEntry.description: One capability above the kernel floor, as this host answers it.

cause.description:
Why not, as a word to match on: `kernel_older`, `not_declared`,
`lsm_inactive`, `not_probed` or `refused`. Absent when active.
`not_probed` says nothing about the kernel.

fallback.description: What runs where it is absent.

hint.description:
How to switch it on here: a kernel to install or a boot parameter to
set. Absent when active, when the probe could not run and when the
kernel refused, since none of those names a change that would help.

id.description: Stable identifier, the same as the metric's `capability` label.

reason.description: Why not, in one sentence. Absent when active.

since.description:
The kernel that introduced what it rests on, or the floor. Used to
word the hint, never to decide `active`.

unlocks.description: What it gives where it is active.

CertificateBody.description: What the server's certificate shows from the wire.

not_after.description: End of validity, in seconds since the epoch, when read.

not_before.description: Start of validity, in seconds since the epoch, when read.

state.description:
`not_observable` in TLS 1.3, where the certificate is encrypted;
`not_captured` in TLS 1.2 when it was not in the bytes read, which is
also what a resumed session gives; `read` when the window below is the
leaf certificate's.

ConfigProvenanceDto.description:
Which configuration document the agent is running, and the policy writes
its API accepted outside that document since the process started.

Whoever wrote the document compares `document_sha256` with the digest of
what they wrote: a difference is a node still on an older document. A
non-zero `runtime_writes` is a node whose policy was changed by hand; a
reload does not clear it, a restart does.

document_sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the document's bytes as last loaded.

loaded_at.description: When that document was loaded, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

runtime_writes.description: Policy writes accepted through the API since the process started.

ConfigSectionWrite.description: One section of the configuration, as the editor holds it.

yaml.description:
A YAML document rooted at the section's own key, exactly as the read
route renders it, so the text an operator edited is the text that
comes back.

max_connections.description:
Conntrack table capacity - the maximum number of flows the
agent tracks before eviction (the BPF connection-table size).

oneOf.description:
The local process that opened the flow, where the socket index could
name one. A flow this node only forwarded has none, and so does one
opened before the hooks attached.

ContainerCoverage.description:
What this agent can say about the containers it sees.

Every field is a verdict rather than a setting: the procfs actually being
read, whether it is the host's, and what each enricher decided.

host_proc.description:
`proc_root` is a mounted host procfs rather than this process's own,
which is what covers a neighbouring container without sharing the
node's pid namespace.

lxc.description: LXC containers: Proxmox CTs, Incus instances and plain LXC.

podman_runtimes.description:
Each Podman runtime the agent has gone to, root's and each user's,
and what it found there. A rootless container whose owner's runtime
is not reachable stays unnamed, and this is where that is said.

proc_root.description: The procfs every container and DLP lookup is rooted on.

resolver.description: The cgroup-id resolver is running, so an alert carries a container id.

ContainerIdentity.description:
Container provenance surfaced on an alert.

The field is absent altogether for a host-namespace process, so `kind` is
always `container` where the object exists at all. It is kept because a
reader that has to tell a container apart from a host should be told so by
a value rather than by an absence it has to interpret.

The Kubernetes and the Docker halves are filled by whichever enricher
attached metadata, and never both, since the pipeline keeps the first
enricher that answered.

container_name.description: Kubernetes container name (only when a k8s enricher attached metadata).

image.description: Image tag (only when the Docker enricher attached metadata).

kind.description: Always `container`: a host-namespace process carries no identity.

name.description: Container name (only when the Docker enricher attached metadata).

namespace.description: Kubernetes namespace (only when a k8s enricher attached metadata).

pod.description: Kubernetes pod name (only when a k8s enricher attached metadata).

runtime.description: Detected runtime (docker, containerd, crio, podman, lxc, unknown).

ContainerLabelEntry.description: One container carrying policy labels, and what came of them.

container_name.description: Container name, when the runtime gave one.

mode.description: `observe` or `enforce`, as the mode label says.

problems.description: What kept its labels out of force.

rules.description:
Identifiers of the workload rules its labels produced, in kernel
order. Empty whenever a problem is listed: a container is policed by
every one of its labels or by none.

ContainerLabelProblem.description: A label of a container that could not be put in force.

label.description:
The label key, or the label prefix when the problem is the
container as a whole.

reason.description: Why it was refused.

ContainerLabelsResponse.description: Every container whose labels carry policy.

closed_by_pod_profile.description:
An agent under the pod profile would see this traffic. Absent when
observed.

gap.description: Why it does not, as a stable code. Absent when observed.

observed.description: The agent's chain sees this traffic.

reason.description: The same reason in a sentence. Absent when observed.

attached.description: Every program of the chain is on the link.

kind.description:
`veth`, `netkit`, `macvlan`, `ipvlan`, `bridge-member`, or the
kernel's own word for a kind the agent does not attach to.

name.description: Interface name in the host namespace.

reason.description: The same reason in a sentence. Absent when attached.

refusal.description: Why it is not, as a stable code. Absent when attached.

health_check_interval_secs.description: Health-check probe interval in seconds. When set, an ICMP probe is configured.

interface.description: Egress interface; defaults to empty (inherits the agent's primary).

weight.description: Routing weight; maps to failover priority (lower = preferred).

listen_addr.description:
Destination address the service answers on, a virtual address.
Omitted, the service answers on every address on its port.

CreateNptV6RuleRequest.description: Request DTO for creating an `NPTv6` prefix translation rule.

vlan_id.description: 802.1Q VLAN ID: omit for any VLAN, 0 for untagged only, 1-4094 exact.

burst_bytes.description: Token bucket depth in bytes. Must be above 0 on a rate-limited pipe.

delay_ms.description: Added latency in milliseconds, paced on egress via the fq qdisc.

direction.description: Which hook the pipe shapes: `ingress`, `egress` or `both`.

rate_bps.description: Bandwidth limit in bits per second; `0` leaves the pipe unlimited.

src_ip.description: Source host to limit, as a bare address or a `/32`.

rate_pps.description: Rate limit in packets per second (required for `throttle_ip`).

target.description:
Target host address (e.g. `1.2.3.4` or `2001:db8::1`). The blacklist
and the rate limiter are both keyed by a single address, so a prefix
is refused rather than silently narrowed.

mode.description:
`enforce` (the default) decides traffic; `shadow` decides nothing and
counts what the rule would have done.

action.description:
`allow`, `permit` or `accept` to permit traffic; `deny`, `drop` or
`reject` to deny it. Any other word is refused.

default_policy.description:
Policy applied when no rule and no inter-zone policy decided the
packet. `allow`, `permit` and `accept` permit; `deny`, `drop` and
`reject` deny, as does an absent value. Any other word is refused.

interfaces.description:
Network interfaces grouped into this zone. A zone with no interface
carries no traffic: the datapath matches on the ingress interface.

name.description: Zone name; used as the zone identifier.

DdosAttackResponse.description: One flood the detector is tracking, or tracked until it expired.

attack_type.description:
`syn_flood`, `udp_amplification`, `icmp_flood`, `rst_flood`,
`fin_flood`, `ack_flood` or `volumetric`: the same spelling the
configuration file uses and `POST /api/v1/ddos/policies` accepts.

last_seen_ns.description:
When the detector last counted a packet against this attack. On the
history route this is where the flood stopped, which a start alone
cannot say.

src_country.description:
Source country, `null` where `GeoIP` resolved none. A policy carrying
`country_thresholds` is judged against this, and a `block` policy
injects this country's CIDRs into the firewall, so an attack with no
country here is one no country rule acted on.

attack_type.description: Spelled the way the configuration file and the create route spell it.

country_thresholds.description:
Per-country thresholds that replace `detection_threshold_pps` for
traffic from those countries, absent where the policy carries none.
Reading it back is the only way to explain a policy that fired well
under the threshold beside it.

DeclaredKfuncEntry.description: One kfunc and whether the kernel declares it.

declared.description: Absent when the kernel's BTF could not be read.

description.description:
What the pattern is for, as the configuration file wrote it. Empty
where none was written.

mode.description:
`alert` or `block`, this pattern's own. A pattern may block while the
service default alerts, so a listing carrying only the service mode
reads as a set of patterns that all merely report.

DlpScopeResponse.description:
What the probes are reading right now.

The effective scope rather than the configured one: it is built from the
workloads the resolvers answered for, so an operator verifies the fence
instead of trusting the document.

allowed_cgroups.description: How many cgroup ids the kernel allow-list carries.

enabled.description: Whether the probes are armed at all.

mode.description:
`all` when every task on the node is read, `workloads` when the
kernel allow-list decides.

refreshed_unix.description: When the scope was last resolved, seconds since the epoch.

selectors.description: How many selectors are in force.

unselected.description:
Workloads seen and named by no rule, counted rather than listed:
on a busy node that list is the node.

DlpScopeUnmatchedResponse.description: A rule that matched nothing, and why.

reason.description: Why it matched nothing, in a sentence an operator can act on.

selector.description: The matchers it carries, as one line.

DlpScopeWorkloadResponse.description: One workload the scope decided on, as the scope route answers it.

cgroup.description: Absolute cgroup v2 path, where one was resolved.

cgroup_id.description: Cgroup id the kernel allow-list carries.

rule.description: The rule that decided it, by name.

DnsRuleReport.description: Which processes may resolve, and what a rule on the DNS ports leaves out.

clients.description: How many workloads may send DNS anywhere, the agent not counted.

not_covered.description:
What the rule does not decide, one sentence each: DNS over HTTPS, a
query handed to a proxy, a resolver on another port, and what a
listed resolver forwards.

ports.description: The destination ports the rule is decided on.

resolvers.description: The resolvers every process may send DNS to, as CIDRs.

enabled.description: Whether DNS intelligence (cache + blocklist) is enabled.

DropReasonBody.description: Packets the kernel dropped for one reason on one interface.

description.description:
What the reason means, in plain language. Absent for a reason the
agent does not describe, which is still counted under its own name.

interface.description:
The device name the packet was on, `if<index>` when the packet had no
device left but remembered the index it arrived on, `none` when it had
neither.

packets.description: Drops counted since the counter was loaded.

reason.description: The reason as the running kernel names it, for instance `NO_SOCKET`.

DropReasonsResponse.description: The kernel's drop counts on this node.

last_error.description:
Why the last read of the counter failed. Absent when it succeeded;
the counts are then the last ones read.

reason.description: Why it is not, in one sentence. Absent when it is.

total.description: Drops counted under a reason and an interface.

uncounted.description:
Drops seen but not counted under a pair, because the kernel-side map
held as many pairs as it can.

encapsulated.description:
The node carries an encapsulating device, so traffic between nodes
crosses the uplink inside an outer header.

full.description: Pods with every class but loopback observed.

links_without_pod.description: Workload links whose owner names no pod the inventory holds.

pod_profile_recommended.description: Pods whose verdict argues for the pod profile.

pods.description: One verdict per pod, uncovered first.

uplinks_attached.description: The chain is on the node's configured interfaces.

attach_blocked.description:
Attaches that lost, if any. `programs[].loaded` says a program is in
the kernel; this says whether it reached the wire.

EnricherState.description:
Where a metadata enricher ended up, as the agent decided it at startup.

The deployment matrix claims container enrichment per mode; this is the
same claim answered by the running agent, so the two can be compared on a
node instead of taken on trust.

ips.description: IP addresses/CIDRs to load into the alias.

last_fetched.description:
Unix-epoch milliseconds of the last completed feed fetch, or `null`
if no fetch has run yet. Shared across feeds (one fetch cycle).

FileKfuncEntry.description: One file kfunc on this host.

declared.description: Whether the kernel's BTF declares it. Absent when the BTF could not be read.

reason.description: The first condition that failed, when it is not usable.

FileKfuncReport.description: What this host answered about the file kfuncs.

probed.description: False until startup has run the probe; every other field is then empty.

remedy.description: The one change on this host that would make them usable, when there is one.

sleepable_lsm.description:
Whether a sleepable LSM program loads. Absent when the probe could not
run, which proves nothing either way.

sleepable_reason.description: Why it does not load, or why nothing was measured.

FingerprintSummaryResponse.description: Response for `GET /api/v1/fingerprints/summary`, the JA4 client fingerprint cache.

persistent.description: Whether the cache is backed by a persistent store that survives restarts.

FlowExportStatusResponse.description: The exporter, its table and its sinks.

enabled.description:
False when no sink is configured, in which case every counter below
is zero because nothing was ever collected, not because nothing
happened.

evicted.description: Flows written out early because the table was full.

queue_drops.description:
Records built and then dropped because the queue to the sinks was
full. A number here is a collector that cannot keep up, and it is why
a missing flow is never a silence.

restarted.description:
Flows whose counters went backwards, which is a five-tuple the kernel
handed to a new connection rather than a negative.

sampled_out.description: Flows the sampling rate left out. Zero at the default rate of one.

sampling.description:
One flow in this many is exported. The collector cannot infer it, so
it has to be configured on both sides.

FlowSinkStatusResponse.description: What one sink says about itself.

detail.description:
Why it is unhealthy, in the words the transport used. Absent while it
is healthy, and it names no address beyond the sink's own name.

healthy.description: False once a write failed and before the next one succeeds.

FqdnNameEntry.description: One name a pattern matched, and what it currently opens.

addresses.description: Distinct addresses currently open for it.

expires_at.description:
Unix seconds its last open address lapses at, absent once every
address it opened has lapsed.

name.description: The name the workload asked for.

refreshed_at.description: Unix seconds of the last answer naming it.

workloads.description: Distinct workloads (cgroups) it is currently open for.

FqdnPatternEntry.description: One pattern of a rule and the names it has resolved.

names.description:
Every name it matched that is still remembered, the most recently
refreshed first. Empty means it never resolved on this node since the
policy was published.

pattern.description: The pattern as the rule wrote it.

FqdnRuleEntry.description: One rule naming its destinations by name.

patterns.description: One entry per pattern, in the rule's order.

health_status.description: Alias of `status` for clients expecting a `health_status` field.

id.description: Gateway identifier, rendered as a string for stable API addressing.

weight.description: Alias of `priority`, exposed as a routing weight.

enabled.description: Whether `GeoIP` enrichment is enabled in the agent configuration.

ready.description: Whether an mmdb-backed lookup database is loaded and ready.

GoExecutableBody.description: One running Go executable and the modules it states.

go_version.description: The toolchain it was built with.

kind.description:
The root of the lowest process running it: `host`, `container` or
`other`.

main_package.description: The import path of its main package.

modules.description: The main module first, then every dependency.

pids.description: Processes running it, lowest first, at most sixteen.

unreadable.description:
Why its build information could not be read. Its modules are then
empty.

GoModuleBody.description: One module a Go executable was linked from.

main.description: Whether it is the module the main package belongs to.

replaced_by.description: What a `replace` directive put in its place, `path version`.

version.description: `(devel)` for a module built from a working tree.

GuestEntry.description: One guest device on this host.

attached.description: Every program of the chain is on the device.

oneOf.description: The guest behind the device. Absent when no record names it.

interface.description: The device in the host namespace.

kind.description:
`tap` or `macvtap`, or `veth` for the link into a KubeVirt launcher
pod.

protection.description: What the agent protects of this guest from the host.

reason.description: The same reason in a sentence. Absent when named.

unnamed.description:
Why no guest is named, as a stable code: `no_source`, `no_record`,
`record_without_name` or `record_unreadable`. Absent when named.

GuestIdentityEntry.description: A guest as its hypervisor names it.

id.description: The libvirt UUID, the Proxmox VMID, or the KubeVirt instance's UID.

name.description:
The libvirt domain name, the Proxmox VM name, or the KubeVirt
`namespace/name`.

tags.description: The hypervisor's tags for the guest; libvirt and KubeVirt keep none.

GuestProtectionEntry.description: What the agent protects of a guest from the host, and why no more.

covered.description:
What is covered: `network` once the chain is on the device, nothing
before.

not_covered.description:
What is not: `process` and `dlp` always, `network` too while the
device is not attached.

reason.description: Why, in a sentence.

guests.description: One entry per guest device, by interface name.

HelperSupportEntry.description: One `(program type, helper)` answer from the startup probe.

HiddenPortBody.description: One port the kernel holds and no listing shows.

address.description: The wildcard the refused bind was made on: `0.0.0.0` or `::`.

host_netns.description: Whether that namespace is the host's.

netns.description: The network namespace, as an inode number.

HiddenPortCountsBody.description: How the last sweep reached its result.

explained_by_listener.description:
Refusals a listed listener explains, every member of a
`SO_REUSEPORT` group included.

explained_by_other_socket.description:
Refusals only another bound socket explains, such as an outgoing
connection.

explained_by_time_wait.description: Refusals only a TCP socket in `TIME_WAIT` explains.

probed.description: Binds attempted in the first pass.

refused.description: Binds refused because the port is in use.

unconfirmed.description:
Refusals the second reading did not confirm: a socket that came or
went between the two.

unprobed.description:
Binds refused for another reason than the port being in use, so the
port was not asked.

unreachable_namespaces.description: Namespaces that could not be entered.

HiddenPortsResponse.description: The last comparison of the socket listings with a bind probe.

last_error.description: Why the last sweep failed. The result is then the sweep before.

probed_ports.description: How many ports each namespace is probed on.

scanned_at_ns.description:
When the last sweep was made, in nanoseconds since the epoch, `0`
before the first.

source.description:
Where the readings come from: `warden` or `local`. Absent when the
sweep is off.

HiddenProcessBody.description: One process that answers a signal and that `/proc` does not list.

comm.description: The command name, where its `/proc` entry could be read.

HiddenProcessCountsBody.description: How the last sweep reached its result.

answered_unlisted.description: Pids that answered and were not listed as a thread group.

explained_by_exit.description: Thread groups on their way out.

explained_by_thread.description: Of those, threads of a listed group.

listed.description: Thread groups the first listing of `/proc` held.

reused.description: Pids that changed hands between the two observations.

unconfirmed.description: Pids gone by the second signal, or listed by the second listing.

HiddenProcessesResponse.description: The last comparison of the listing of `/proc` with a signal sweep.

last_error.description:
Why the last sweep failed or was not taken. The result is then the
sweep before.

pids_per_second.description: The pace asked for, in pids a second.

scanned_at_ns.description:
When the last sweep was made, in nanoseconds since the epoch, `0`
before the first.

source.description:
Where the readings come from: `warden` or `local`. Absent when the
sweep is off.

HostIntentsResponse.description: Every intention a host rule may name, resolved against this host.

applicable.description: How many of the intentions this host serves.

kernel.description: The running kernel as `major.minor`, absent when it could not be read.

mode.description:
`shadow`, counting what it would have done and doing none of it, or
`enforce`, acting on what it matches.

oneOf.description: What it would have done, for a rule in shadow.

spec.description: The rule as it was written, `workload` and `when` included.

state.description:
`applicable` when every intention it names is served here,
`partially_applicable` when some are, `not_applicable` when none is.

then.description: `alert`, and `kill_process` where the rule stops the process.

HostRuleExceptionBody.description: A workload some host rules leave alone.

rules.description: The rules it silences; empty for every rule.

workload.description: The workload it names, written as a rule's `workload`.

HostRulesResponse.description: Every loaded host rule, and what they have matched since the start.

counting.description: Groups a count is running for now.

counting_refused.description:
Events not counted because the groups or the events held were at
their bound.

dropped.description: Of the matches of rules in force, alerts lost to a full alert queue.

exempted.description: Matches an exception left alone: no alert and no shadow reading.

matched.description: Events that matched a rule, in force or in shadow.

pending.description: First steps of sequences waiting for their second now.

pending_refused.description:
First steps not held because the bounded set of waiting ones was
full.

shadow_since_ns.description:
When the shadow readings started, nanoseconds since the epoch: the
agent's start.

HostShadowBody.description: What a rule in shadow would have done since the reading started.

events.description: Events on which it would have acted.

unsampled.description: Events about a workload that came after the sample was full.

workloads.description: Those events by workload, the first ones seen, bounded.

HostShadowWorkloadBody.description: Events a shadow rule would have acted on about one workload.

workload.description:
The container, else the cgroup, else the systemd unit; absent for a
process in none of them.

country_thresholds.description:
Per-country threshold overrides, keyed by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. A
rule stricter for one country reads as a single threshold without
them.

domain_pattern.description:
Domain the rule matches on, for rules evaluated against resolved names
rather than against a port.

interfaces.description:
The interface groups this rule is scoped to, in the words the
configuration file used, `!` prefix included. Empty is a floating
rule, which sees every interface the classifier is attached to.

oneOf.description:
Present only when another rule holds a kernel map slot this rule also
claims.

src_port.description:
Source-port match, set on rules watching the reply leg of a flow. A
rule carrying one fires on nothing else, so a listing that dropped it
read as matching every port.

workload.description:
The workload this rule is scoped to, written out the way the
firewall's workload rules are. Absent is a rule that inspects every
workload.

go_programs.description: Running Go programs, whose modules no database lists.

packages.description: Packages the databases list, every root together.

roots_not_read.description: Roots that could not be read.

IntentBody.description: One intention and whether this host serves it.

fallback.description: What serves it, less well, when the hook is absent.

hook.description: The kernel mechanism serving it, in one line.

min_kernel.description: Oldest kernel the hook exists on, as `major.minor`.

name.description: The name a rule writes, such as `process.connects`.

reason.description: Why this host cannot serve it, one sentence per missing source.

sources.description: The sources it needs, every one of them.

interfaces.description:
The interface groups this rule is scoped to, in the words the
configuration file used, `!` prefix included. Empty is a floating
rule, which enforces on every interface the classifier is on.

oneOf.description:
Present only when another rule holds a kernel map slot this rule also
claims. A prevention rule that lost its slot is never replayed in
userspace, so it blocks nothing until the conflict is resolved.

kill_process.description:
The rule also stops the process behind a flow it blocks. Present only
when it does.

KernelFeaturesResponse.description:
What the kernel answered when the agent probed it at startup.

`probed = false` means the probe could not run, **not** that the kernel
lacks anything: `helpers` and `missing_required` are then empty because
nothing was measured, and `reason` says why. Treating that as a capability
report would invert its meaning.

attribution.description:
Whether the socket-attribution hooks are on this host's cgroup, and
why not where they are not. Read from what the attach actually did,
not from the probe: a kernel that supports the program type can still
refuse the attach, and a flow with no workload on it is the same
silence either way.

bpf_lsm.description:
Whether an LSM program can attach on this host. Read from the host
rather than from any attach, because it is asked before anything that
needs it is configured, and the kernel version does not answer it.

capabilities.description:
Every capability above the kernel floor, active or not, with why not
and how to switch it on. The blocks above are the detail each probe
or attach gives; this is the one answer an estate compares host by
host. A capability is active on evidence from this host, never because
of the kernel's version.

file_kfuncs.description:
Whether the kfuncs that read a task's executable and a file's path
and attributes are usable here. Each is declared or not by the
kernel's BTF, and usable only where a sleepable LSM program loads and
the BPF LSM is active, so the report says which of the three failed.

kfunc_features.description:
Kernel facts no shipped program uses yet, each with what it would be
used for, so the day one is wired this host's answer is already here.

load_mode.description:
How the agent loads its objects, which is why a probe needing
`CAP_BPF` can be unavailable on a host where every program loads.

network_executables.description:
Whether the kernel decides which executables reach the network, and
whether it refuses or only reports. Reported whether or not the list is
configured, with the reason it is not in force.

process_signal.description:
Whether this node can stop the process behind a flow, and with what.
Reported whether or not the capability is on, because the blast radius
of an action has to be readable before somebody arms it.

process_tracing.description:
Whether the exec and exit tracepoints behind the process table are on
this host, and why not where they are not. Read the same way as the
attribution block above: from what the attach did.

quarantine.description:
Whether this node can cut a workload off the network while leaving it
running, and whether that cut reaches the flows it already holds.
Reported whether or not the capability is on, for the same reason as
the block above.

self_protection.description:
Whether the kernel refuses every other task a writable descriptor to
the agent's maps and a descriptor to its links. A node without the
BPF LSM says it is unprotected and why, rather than saying nothing.

workload_firewall.description:
Whether the hooks deciding a workload rule are on this host's cgroup.
Read the same way as the two blocks above, and asked more often than
either: a rule naming a binary is the one kind of rule whose absence
nothing on the wire makes visible.

write_refusal.description:
Whether the kernel refuses a write-open past a count under the
watched data paths, or the first by an unexpected executable under
the system paths, and whether it refuses or only counts. Reported
whether or not it is configured, with the reason it is not in force.

KfuncFeatureEntry.description: One kernel fact, the kfuncs it rests on and what it would be used for.

consumer.description: What the agent would use it for.

load_tested.description: Whether a program was loaded to confirm it, or the BTF alone was read.

reason.description: Why it is not confirmed, in one sentence.

usable.description:
True when a load confirmed it, false when the kernel lacks or refused
it, absent when nothing could confirm it either way.

KfuncFeaturesReport.description: What this host answered about the kfuncs a future program would rest on.

probed.description: False until startup has run the probe; `features` is then empty.

dst_ip_alias.description: The same, on the destination address.

dst_port_alias.description: The same, on the destination port.

src_country_codes.description:
ISO-3166 country codes the rule narrows its source to. A rule scoped
to a handful of countries and served without them reads as a rule
acting on every source there is.

src_ip_alias.description:
The alias the rule was declared against, in the words the
configuration file used, so a reader can find the line that wrote it.
A rule created through this API names none.

probed.description:
Whether anything ever measured the status above. A backend of a service
with no health check, a disabled backend and a backend of a disabled
service are never probed, and each of them reads `healthy` for ever.

LbHealthCheckResponse.description:
What a service is probed with, in the words the configuration file used.

The probe carries no target of its own: every enabled backend is reached on
the address and port it serves on.

oneOf.description:
The probe behind the backend statuses below, omitted where the service
carries none and nothing is ever measured.

listen_addr.description:
Destination address the service answers on, omitted when it answers
on every address on its port.

health_checked.description:
Whether the service carries a health check at all. A backend of a
service that carries none starts healthy and is never probed, so its
status is a default rather than a measurement.

listen_addr.description:
Destination address the service answers on, omitted when it answers
on every address on its port.

interface.description: L2 interface VIPs egress on. Required unless role is disabled.

vips.description:
VIPs this node owns. Must be non-empty unless role is disabled,
and ignored when it is.

error.description: Why the last push to, or read of, the BGP daemon failed.

exporting.description: Whether this node exports a route for its VIPs right now.

since.description: When the session entered that state, as the daemon reports it.

state.description:
`Idle`, `Connect`, `Active`, `OpenSent`, `OpenConfirm`,
`Established`, or `Down` when the daemon holds it switched off.

seconds.description:
How long this node speaks for its VIPs unless renewed, in seconds,
at most 300. Zero releases the role at once.

arp_replies.description:
Forged ARP replies emitted for this VIP since program load
(per-CPU summed kernel counter).

self_announced.description:
Whether this VIP is currently in the self-whitelist (true when
the node is speaker and the binding has been written).

bindings_count.description:
Number of self-owned bindings registered in the kernel
`SELF_OWNED_BINDINGS` map.

grant_remaining_ms.description:
Milliseconds left on the speaker grant of an `elected` node, absent
when it holds none. The node falls silent when this reaches zero
without a renewal.

interface.description: L2 interface VIPs egress on (empty when role is disabled).

is_speaker.description: Whether this node currently answers ARP / sends gratuitous ARP.

LearningEdgeBody.description: One thing a workload reached during the window.

observations.description:
Samples it was seen in: how persistent the edge was, not how many
connections were opened.

addresses.description:
The addresses each workload dialled from, which is how a reader
holding several nodes' windows recognises an edge's destination as a
workload rather than an address.

edges.description: Every edge, by workload, then address, then port.

session.description: The window, as it stood at the reading.

collapsed_rules.description:
Rules whose destination was widened to a prefix. Each one names the
addresses it came from in a comment above it.

rules.description: Rules written, the closing deny of each workload included.

session.description: The window it was rendered from, as it stood at the reading.

skipped_edges.description:
Destinations no rule could be written for, because their workload
cannot be named by a selector.

yaml.description: The document, YAML in the agent's own rule schema.

LearningSegmentationResponse.description:
The rules segmenting the containers on the node's bridges, with what it
took to write them.

bridges.description: Bridges that carried at least one container.

containers.description: Containers given rules, counted once per bridge they sit on.

peer_rules.description: Rules letting a container through to a peer on its bridge.

session.description: The window it was rendered from, as it stood at the reading.

unlearned.description: Containers on a bridge the window never saw, which get no rule.

unnamed.description: Containers the window saw under a name no rule can select them by.

yaml.description: The document, YAML in the agent's own rule schema.

LearningSessionResponse.description:
A window, as it stands.

Everything a reader needs to decide whether the document it would
produce is worth applying: how long it has really been watching, whether
the agent was up for all of it, how many destinations it holds, how many
it had to refuse, and how long since it last found a new one.

continuous.description: False once the agent has been down for part of the window.

dropped_edges.description:
Destinations refused because the window was full. Anything but zero
means the document it produces is incomplete, and it says so.

gap_secs.description: Seconds of the window the agent was not running for.

scope_description.description: The scope in one line, as the generated document states it.

LearningWorkloadAddressesBody.description: The local addresses one workload dialled from during the window.

LearningWorkloadBody.description:
How a window names a workload: `container`, `unit` or `executable`, and
the name under that kind.

ListenerBody.description: One address and port a process accepts traffic on.

accepted.description:
TCP connections accepted on it since the hooks attached. Absent for
UDP, which has no handshake to count.

address.description: The bound address, `0.0.0.0` or `::` for every address.

allowed_from.description:
The sources let through, when only some are. Absent means every
source when `reachable`, and none when not.

bound_at_boot_ns.description: When the first of its sockets was bound, in nanoseconds since boot.

class.description:
`exposed_used`, `exposed_unused`, `exposed_unmeasured` (UDP, whose use
is not counted), `closed_by_policy` or `loopback_only`.

container.description: The container holding it, where it runs in one.

decided_by.description:
What decided `reachable`: `rule`, `default_policy`,
`firewall_not_enforcing` (disabled or in alert mode) or `loopback`.

executable.description: Its executable, where the process table holds it.

last_accepted_boot_ns.description: When the last of them was accepted, in nanoseconds since boot.

pod.description: The pod holding it, as `namespace/name`, where it runs in one.

reachable.description: Whether the packet firewall lets anything off the node through to it.

scope.description:
`all_addresses` when bound on every address of the namespace,
`address` for one interface address, `loopback` when nothing off the
node reaches it.

sockets.description:
Sockets the process holds on this address and port, more than one
for a server spread over `SO_REUSEPORT`.

unit.description: The systemd unit holding it, for a host process.

ListenersResponse.description:
The sockets this node accepts traffic on, who bound them, who may reach
them and whether anybody did.

listeners.description: Widest scope first: every address, then one address, then loopback.

reading.description:
Whether the socket hooks are attached. When they are not, the node's
listeners are unknown rather than absent.

ListeningBody.description: One listener and the packages behind it.

accepted.description:
TCP connections accepted on it since the hooks attached; absent for
UDP.

allowed_from.description: The sources let through, when only some are.

class.description:
`exposed_used`, `exposed_unused`, `exposed_unmeasured`,
`closed_by_policy` or `loopback_only`, as on the listeners route.

mapped_read.description:
Whether the files its process maps were read. When not, the two
lists below are unknown rather than empty.

origin.description:
Who the policy lets reach it: `anywhere`, `private_only` when every
source let through lies in a private or link-local range,
`blocked` or `loopback`.

packages.description: The packages owning a file its process maps, each once.

unowned.description: Files its process maps that no package in its root owns.

ListeningResponse.description: Every listener with the packages its process maps.

inventory_read.description: Whether the package inventory is read.

listeners_read.description: Whether the socket hooks are attached.

inventory_read.description: Whether the package inventory is read.

listeners_read.description: Whether the socket hooks are attached.

reachable.description:
Every listener something off the node may reach, with the packages
behind it.

scanned_at_ns.description:
When the inventory was last read, nanoseconds since the epoch, `0`
before the first.

keyword.description: The keyword, or part of the rule header, that stopped it.

line.description: The line of the ruleset the rule starts on, counted from 1.

reason.description: One sentence of why.

sid.description: The rule's sid, absent when the rule was refused before one was read.

SuricataReportResponse.description: What the configured Suricata rulesets compiled to.

rulesets.description:
One entry per ruleset, in the order the configuration names them.
Empty when no ruleset is imported.

SuricataRulesetResponse.description: One ruleset's import: what loaded, and every refusal with its reason.

disabled.description: Rules present but commented out, which are not read.

native_rules.description: Detection rules the compiled ones became, one per port they name.

refused_by_keyword.description: Refusals counted by the keyword that caused them, most frequent first.

refused_share.description: The share of enabled rules refused, from 0 to 1.

source.description: The ruleset file, as the configuration names it.

total.description: Rules the ruleset enables, compiled or not.

TechniqueEntry.description: A single technique in the coverage matrix.

ThresholdResponse.description: Per-rule threshold/rate detection, surfaced for rate-based IDS rules.

TlsHandshakeBody.description: One TLS handshake seen on the node.

cipher.description: The selected cipher suite's code point.

cipher_name.description: Its IANA name, absent for a suite this agent does not name.

group.description:
The selected key exchange group's code point, absent when the
exchange has none or it was not in the bytes read.

group_name.description: Its IANA name, absent for a group this agent does not name.

observed_at_ns.description: When the server's flight was read, in nanoseconds since the epoch.

version.description: The negotiated version as the wire carries it (`772` is TLS 1.3).

version_name.description: Its name, absent for a value this agent does not name.

capacity.description: How many handshakes the log keeps before dropping the oldest.

recording.description: Whether this agent reads TLS handshakes at all.

TlsPostureResponse.description: The cryptographic posture of each edge since the agent started.

evicted_edges.description: Edges dropped, least recently seen first, to make room for new ones.

totals.description: The node's connections, every edge summed.

TlsStatusResponse.description:
Per-connection TLS status, surfaced so operators can confirm the
negotiated key-exchange group (e.g. verify a post-quantum hybrid
handshake) on a live connection.

negotiated_group.description:
Negotiated TLS 1.3 key-exchange named group for this connection
(e.g. `X25519MLKEM768`, `X25519`, `secp256r1`), or `null` when the
request did not arrive over TLS.

post_quantum.description:
`true` when the negotiated group is the post-quantum hybrid
(`X25519MLKEM768`).

tls.description: Whether this request arrived over TLS.

dst_port.description: Destination port, required for TCP and UDP.

src_ip.description: Source address. Left out when `workload` names the source.

src_port.description: Source port; zero or absent picks an ephemeral port. Ignored for ICMP.

workload.description: A pod as `namespace/name`, whose address becomes the source.

not_loaded.description:
Programs of this direction that are not loaded, so the trace could
not ask them.

src_ip.description: The source address the packet was crafted from.

stages.description: Each stage the packet crossed, in the order it crossed them.

state_dependent.description:
Verdicts that hold for this packet now and not for every packet of
the five-tuple.

stopped_at.description: The stage the packet stopped at, absent when it went through.

verdict.description: The verdict at that stage, or `pass` when the packet went through.

detail.description: What the stage adds in its own terms.

reason.description:
Why the stage decided: `default`, `rule`, `established`, `rate`,
`list`, `malformed`, `disabled`, `rewrite` or `unrecorded`.

rule.description: The rule's name, where the agent could name it.

rule_id.description: The rule identifier as the stage numbers its rules.

depends_on.description: The state the verdict depends on, in a sentence.

TriageRequest.description:
`PATCH /api/v1/alerts/{id}/triage` body. A field left out stays as it
was; `assignee: null` takes the alert off whoever held it.

author.description:
Who is writing, when a console writes on a person's behalf.
Defaults to the authenticated identity.

TriageResponse.description: The triage of one alert after a change.

UnreachableNamespaceBody.description: A namespace that could not be entered, so nothing in it was asked.

UprobeEntry.description: One uprobe the DLP module currently holds a link for.

brokered.description:
`BPF_LINK_CREATE` was issued by the warden (rootless posture) rather than
by the agent itself.

dev.description: Block device of the probed file.

ino.description:
Inode of the probed file. With `dev`, the identity two runs are compared
on: the same path can name a different file after a package upgrade.

offset.description:
File offset the link was created at. A changed offset for an unchanged
inode is a resolution regression, not a new build.

path.description: Path the link was created against, as the loader saw it.

program.description: Loader name of the eBPF program behind the probe.

retprobe.description: The probe fires on return rather than on entry.

sticky.description:
The attachment survives a reconcile that finds no process mapping the
inode - the cold-start system-library fallback.

symbol.description: Exported symbol the probe sits on.

UprobeInventoryResponse.description:
The uprobe set the DLP module currently holds.

An empty list is a real answer, and always the same one: no TLS payload is
being read. It covers a DLP module that is not loaded, a scan that resolved
nothing, and a datapath that has been detached.

probes.description: Every probe, ordered by inode then symbol so two runs diff cleanly.

WorkloadAncestorResponse.description: One process above the one behind a flow.

exe.description: The executable path, where the process table read one.

exited.description: It has exited and is kept because this process descends from it.

pid.description: The ancestor's pid when it ran.

start_ns.description: Kernel monotonic start time in nanoseconds, where the kernel read it.

WorkloadAncestryResponse.description: The chain above the process behind a flow, parent first, at most eight.

incomplete.description:
The chain stops at an ancestor that was named and that the table does
not hold, rather than at the root.

truncated.description: The chain goes on past the last ancestor listed.

WorkloadFirewallReport.description: What became of the workload firewall hooks on this host.

attached.description:
True only when every hook attached. There is no optional hook here:
half the hooks is a policy that reads as in force and is not.

brokered.description: Whether the warden created the links, which is the rootless posture.

cgroup.description: The cgroup the hooks were attached to, or asked for.

oneOf.description:
The rule on the DNS ports, absent while `firewall.dns_clients` is
off. Carries what it does not see in the same answer, so a policy on
two ports never reads as a policy on DNS as a whole.

hooks.description: The hooks that attached, named as the kernel programs are.

reason.description:
Why nothing is attached, in the words the attach failed with. A
document carrying no workload rule loads no object, and says so here.

WorkloadFqdnResponse.description: What every rule naming a destination by name has resolved on this node.

WorkloadReachEntry.description: One rule naming the workload, and what it has refused.

allows.description: Whether the rule lets the destination through.

decided_at.description:
For a rule naming a workload on another node: `both` when the node
a connection arrives at decides it too, `source` when only the node
it leaves can.

denials.description:
How many socket operations this rule has refused since it was
published, counted by the kernel.

destination.description: The destination half of the match, written out.

mode.description: `enforce` when the kernel refuses, `observe` when it only counts.

selector.description: The selector written out, as the rule names the workload.

source_only_reason.description: Why the node a connection arrives at cannot decide it.

WorkloadReachResponse.description: The answer to "what may this workload reach".

enforcing.description: Whether any rule in force has the kernel refuse rather than count.

exe.description:
The facts the rules were matched against, after the process table
filled in whatever the caller did not give.

rules.description:
Every rule naming this workload, in the order the kernel walks them.
The first one admitting the destination decides, so a rule low in
this list is a rule something above it may never reach.

WorkloadResponse.description: The process a flow belongs to, where the agent could name one.

oneOf.description: The processes above this one, where the process table holds any.

cgroup.description: cgroup v2 id, as the kernel numbers it.

command_line.description:
The command line, where the operator turned its capture on. The
secret-bearing shapes were removed where argv was read, before it was
stored, so what is here is what every reader of the process table saw.

container.description: Container id, where the process runs in one.

exe.description:
The executable path the process table recorded. Forgeable by the
process itself, which is why it is a path and not an identity.

exe_hash.description:
Digest of the executable, which is what names the bytes rather than
the place: `fsverity-sha256:<hex>` where the kernel measured a file
with fs-verity on, `sha256:<hex>` where the agent read its contents.
Absent where the agent could not open the file.

image.description: Container image, where the runtime enricher read one.

oneOf.description:
The workload at the other end of the flow, where its address is on
another node of the fleet. Named from the list the console hands this
node, never read off the wire.

pid.description:
The process that owns the socket. Never zero: a block exists only
when there is a process to name.

pod.description: Pod name, on a Kubernetes node.

service_account.description: Service account the pod runs as, where the enricher read one.

source.description:
How the process was reached - `socket` when the kernel's own handle
on the socket answered, `flow` when the five-tuple was matched
against the index of established connections, `process` when the
event already named the task. The first and the third are read, the
second is correlated.

uid.description: The real uid of the task when the socket was opened.

unit.description: systemd unit, for a host process the agent could place in one.

WorkloadRulesResponse.description: The workload rules in force, each with what it has refused.

enforcing.description: Whether any rule in force has the kernel refuse rather than count.

rules.description: Every rule in force, in the order the kernel walks them.

WorkloadSelectorBody.description:
One of the selectors a scope is written with, in the shape a workload
rule already uses.

WriteRefusalReport.description: What became of the write refusal on this host.

attached.description: Both hooks are attached and deciding.

directories.description: How many watched paths the kernel holds, both regimes.

enforcing.description: A writer past the threshold is refused rather than counted.

expected_writers.description: How many expected writers of the system paths the kernel holds.

marks.description: How many inode marks the fanotify route holds; zero on the BPF LSM.

reason.description: Why the refusal is not in force, in one sentence.

route.description:
Which mechanism refuses: `bpf_lsm`, or `fanotify` where the BPF LSM
is not active. Absent while nothing does.

system_paths.description:
How many of them are system paths, refused at the first write by an
executable not expected there.

WriteRefusalShadowResponse.description: The write refusal's mode and the writes it would have refused in shadow.

counting_since_ns.description:
When this reading started, boot-time nanoseconds. A promotion names it,
and is refused if the reading started again since.

enabled.description: Whether a refusal runs here, on either route.

mode.description:
`shadow`, counting the writers that reached the threshold and refusing
nothing, or `enforce`, refusing their next open; absent where no
refusal runs.

recent.description: The last of them as the alert would have read, newest last.

shadow.description: The writes it would have refused, by the workload of the writer.

action.description: Alias of `policy`, exposed under the `action` field name.

api_key.name: X-API-Key
api_key.description: Static API key configured in agent

bearer_auth.description: JWT token obtained via OIDC or static configuration
